questions.q: Which Event Monitoring tool is genuinely real-time, capable of flagging unusual activity as it happens rather than after a delay?
options: Event Log Files
Event Log Objects
Setup Audit Trail
Real-Time Event Monitoring
questions.explain: Real-Time Event Monitoring uses statistical/anomaly-detection methods to flag unusual activity as it happens -- Event Log Files and Event Log Objects are both after-the-fact or near-real-time with a delay, not truly instantaneous.

questions.q: A compliance team wants a comprehensive, after-the-fact report covering every login and export event across the org for the past year. Which tool best fits this need?
options: Event Log Files
Real-Time Event Monitoring
Transaction Security Policies
Field Audit Trail
questions.explain: Event Log Files are comprehensive, interval-generated logs covering many event types, purpose-built for thorough historical/after-the-fact analysis -- exactly a year-end compliance report's use case.

questions.q: What makes Transaction Security Policies categorically different from Event Log Files, Event Log Objects, and Real-Time Event Monitoring?
options: They are cheaper and require no Shield license
They can take an actual action (notify, block, force step-up authentication, freeze the user, end the session) when conditions are met, rather than only observing and recording activity
They only work on Sandbox orgs, never Production
They replace the need for any of the other three tools entirely
questions.explain: The other three tools are observational -- they record or surface what happened or is happening. Transaction Security Policies are a rules engine that can act on a real-time event, closing the detection-to-response loop automatically.

questions.q: Why does this lesson warn that the sentence "we have Event Monitoring enabled" doesn't tell you much on its own?
options: Because Event Monitoring is not a real Salesforce feature
Because Event Monitoring only applies to Developer Edition orgs

Because there are three distinct tools (Event Log Files, Event Log Objects, Real-Time Event Monitoring) with very different speed and use cases, so the sentence doesn't specify which capability -- historical reconstruction or actual in-progress detection -- is actually in place
Because enabling Event Monitoring automatically enables Transaction Security Policies as well
questions.explain: The three tools answer very different questions at very different speeds -- an architect has to ask specifically which one(s) are in play rather than assuming "Event Monitoring" means real-time detection capability exists.

questions.q: Per this lesson's starter-policy description, what is one example of a default policy an org typically gets when enabling Transaction Security Policies?
options: A policy that automatically encrypts every field in the org
A policy that deletes Event Log Files older than 24 hours
A policy that disables all API access permanently
A policy limiting concurrent login sessions, or a policy limiting bulk data exports -- each backed by a customizable Apex class
questions.explain: Enabling Transaction Security typically provides starter policies such as a concurrent-session-limit policy and a bulk-export-limit policy, each backed by an Apex class the architect can customize rather than being a fixed, uneditable rule.
